stepBody: Mr. Bean increases the number of trained models to $$100$$ and evaluates the models on the point $$(x_i,y_i).$$ Using historical data, he assumes that measurement errors follow a normal distribution with mean $$0$$ and standard deviation $$\sigma=4$$ mm. Given the statistics from pd.describe on the predictions and loss for these models (preds mean $$=$$ $$104.130417$$, preds std $$=$$ $$8.255889$$, MSE mean $$=$$ $$101.930101)$$, estimate the magnitude of the empirical bias. Round to $$3$$ decimal places.\n\nHint: Think of how bias is calculated in our bias-variance decomposition: $$E[(y-f_{\theta}(x))**{2}]=\sigma**{2}+Var[f_{\theta}(x)]+(E[f_{\theta}(x)]-g(x))**{2}$$##figure5.gif##
